name: duration-picker
purpose: Enter a fixed-length, non-negative Duration (milliseconds) in contiguous unit segments (days, hours, minutes, seconds; default hours and minutes) inside a labelled group. Each segment is a spinbutton with localized unit text; ArrowUp/ArrowDown change the total and carry between units, with min, max, and step validation and native form submission as an ISO 8601 duration (PT1H30M).
whenToUse: An amount of elapsed or planned time: a task estimate, a timeout, a meeting length, a lap or cooking time.
Values that users think of in several units at once (1 h 30 min) rather than as one number of minutes.
Durations that must stay on a grid (for example quarter hours) or within bounds.
whenNotToUse: A time of day (09:30): use Time Picker; a duration has no clock position.
Calendar periods such as months or years, whose length depends on the start date: not supported; use Number Input with a unit, or a date range.
Negative durations or offsets (for example -5 min): not supported.
A single unit with a large range (for example 0-10,000 seconds): Number Input is simpler.
Sub-second precision: the smallest unit is seconds.
responsive: The group hugs its unit segments up to 100% of the container; units wrap inside the group in very narrow containers. Segment widths use ch units with tabular digits; the largest segment is wider for extra digits. Density tokens adjust the control height.
rtl: The group uses the direction option (or the inherited global direction), so units flow right to left in RTL. ArrowLeft/ArrowRight move between units following the reading direction (mirrored in RTL). Unit text is placed before or after the number as the locale's Intl unit formatting does.
theme: Control surface, border, focus, error, selected, disabled, and sunken-surface role tokens. The group shows the focus indicator while any segment is focused; the focused segment uses the selected pair. Forced-colors mode outlines the focused group with Highlight, uses Highlight/HighlightText for the focused segment, and GrayText for disabled unit text.
timezone: Not applicable. A Duration (SPEC section 8.4) is a fixed number of milliseconds with no date, clock position, or timezone; the component does not inherit the timezone option. A day is exactly 24 hours, so daylight-saving transitions never change a value.
security: Label, help text, unit text, value texts, and messages are rendered with textContent. Validation messages never include the entered value; range and step messages include only the configured bounds and step. CSP-safe: no inline styles or HTML.
dataHandling: No persistence, network access, or telemetry. A hidden input carries the ISO 8601 duration in hours, minutes, and seconds (PT1H30M; a day and two hours is PT26H, because days are never emitted) for native form submission when `name` is set; it is empty while the entry is empty or invalid, and disabled (not submitted) while the picker is disabled.

performance.testedScale: Up to four unit segments per instance; the largest segment holds up to the digits of max (default 3 digits for days and hours, 4 for minutes, 5 for seconds).

limitations: Negative durations are not supported; value, min, and max must be non-negative.
Calendar durations (years, months, weeks) are not supported; a day is always 24 hours.
The value and step must be whole numbers of the smallest unit in fields; milliseconds cannot be entered.
Without max, the largest segment is limited by its digits (999 days, 999 hours, 9,999 minutes, or 99,999 seconds).
Only ASCII digits are accepted in segments; locale digits (for example Arabic-Indic) are not parsed.
No popup or preset list; values are typed or stepped.
Screen-reader behavior has not yet been manually verified with NVDA, JAWS, and VoiceOver.
unsupported: Rendering HTML in the label, help text, or messages.
Non-contiguous fields (for example days and minutes without hours).
Negative or calendar durations; ISO 8601 day, week, month, or year designators in the form value.
antiPatterns: Using a Duration Picker for a time of day or an end time; use Time Picker, or derive the end from a start and a duration.
Adding a Duration of whole days to a date as if every calendar day were 24 hours across a DST change.
Showing seconds when users only ever need minutes; extra segments slow entry.

adapters.angular: @absoluteui/angular/duration-picker: AuiDurationPicker directive ([auiDurationPicker]) with ControlValueAccessor and Validator.
adapters.react: @absoluteui/react/duration-picker: AuiDurationPicker component; controlled (value/defaultValue + onValueChange) or uncontrolled.
